introduction: The urban planning of the Indus Valley Civilization is considered one of the most advanced and well-organized systems in the ancient world. It reflects not only antiquity but also scientific thinking and administrative efficiency. At this level, we will logically understand city structure, drainage systems, and architecture.

core_concepts.title: Grid Pattern
core_concepts.description: The streets of Indus cities were laid out in straight lines, intersecting each other at right angles in north-south and east-west directions, dividing the city into rectangular blocks. This resembles modern city planning.

core_concepts.title: Well-Organized Drainage System
core_concepts.description: Water from each house flowed through covered drains into larger main drains, which carried it outside the city. The drains were well-covered to ensure cleanliness and easy maintenance.

core_concepts.title: Great Bath
core_concepts.description: Located at Mohenjo-daro, it was a large public bathing structure used for religious or social purposes. It was constructed using waterproof bricks.

core_concepts.title: Citadel and Lower Town
core_concepts.description: Each major city was divided into two parts: the upper citadel, which housed administrative and religious buildings, and the lower town, where common people lived.

core_concepts.title: Standardized Building Material
core_concepts.description: Burnt bricks of a uniform ratio (1:2:4) were used across the civilization, ensuring uniformity and structural strength.

important_entities.name: Mohenjo-daro
important_entities.significance: Famous for the Great Bath and advanced drainage system

important_entities.name: Harappa
important_entities.significance: Known for granaries and organized city planning

important_entities.name: Dholavira
important_entities.significance: Unique three-part city layout and water conservation system

important_entities.name: Lothal
important_entities.significance: Famous for its dockyard and role as a trade center

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume all metals were used, but the Indus Civilization used only copper and bronze; iron was unknown.
Although most cities followed a grid pattern, cities like Dholavira had unique layouts, so assuming all cities were identical is incorrect.
The Great Bath has been found only at Mohenjo-daro, not in other cities.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: This helps remember that cities were divided into an upper citadel and a lower residential area.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: House to drain, drain to outside
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Water moved from individual houses to smaller drains and then to main drains outside the city.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Mohenjo bath, Harappa grain, Lothal dock, Dholavira unique
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Mohenjo-daro - Great Bath, Harappa - Granary, Lothal - Dockyard, Dholavira - Unique structure

exam_strategy_tips: In questions related to urban planning, keywords like 'drainage system' and 'grid pattern' are very important.
If you see 'use of iron' in options, immediately consider it incorrect.
